chapter: Pure Year 2 Chapter 2 — Functions and graphs
visualReview: All 94 referenced original question/answer diagrams inspected. All 69 original prompts and supplied final answers compared. Every row renders with strict KaTeX, no mathematical failures, missing images or horizontal overflow; representative inverse, modulus and new exact graph renders inspected. Source and solution top-level subpart counts match for every row. Full Papers print integration remains separate.

suppliedPromptOrKeyDefects.note: The line ends at an open point (2,4); the parabola starts at a closed point (2,6) and has vertex (4,2). Each real input belongs to exactly one branch, so it has one output. The supplied answer incorrectly calls this mapping one-to-one; for example f(3)=f(5)=3.

The exact range is (−∞,k+4], not the open interval (−∞,6). Read literally as equality of ranges, the wording has no solution; the intended strict upper-bound condition gives k<2 with k=0 excluded by the question.

The parabola opens upward, crossing at (−3,0),(1,0),(0,−3). Part (i) has three turning points: the central maximum (−1,10) and two cusp minima (−3,2),(1,2). The supplied answer lists only the transformed original vertex.

The endpoint x=2 is excluded: the supplied answer incorrectly includes it. The minimum 2 is approached but never attained; the supplied non-strict bound is incorrect. The supplied extra root −11 is outside the domain of g.
The original answer sketches incorrectly label the y-intercept 1. These sketches use the stated formula and the correct value 2.

The given original expression also excludes x=3, despite the statement saying only x>2. T₁ translates by (2,0), T₂ reflects in the x-axis, and T₃ translates by (0,2). These map to the continuous extension of the simplified curve. The literal original function has a hole at (3,1); no three ordinary affine transformations of the full starting branch create that missing point.
